title: Verify slopes, crowns and grades
intro: Grade work turns a drawing into reliable elevations on the ground. Keep the benchmark, units, drawing revision and sign convention visible in every calculation. Another person should be able to repeat your result without guessing what a number means.

sections.title: Confirm plans/blueprints
sections.text: Read the title block, north arrow, legend, scale, revision and detail references before measuring. A plan is the overhead view; a profile follows an alignment; a cross-section cuts across it. Profiles often exaggerate the vertical scale, so the drawn angle is not the road’s actual slope. Use stated dimensions before scaling, especially on resized screens or prints. One inch is exactly 25.4 mm and one foot exactly 0.3048 m. Horizontal run is used for ordinary grade calculations; a tape stretched along a slope measures a longer distance.

sections.title: Define role of Surveyor
sections.text: The surveyor establishes or verifies control and supplies elevations, alignment and construction information within their assigned role. Cut and fill at a profile station normally refer to the defined centreline, not automatically to the entire cross-section. Pipe invert is the inside-bottom elevation. Depth to invert and cover above the pipe crown are different quantities; calculating cover requires the appropriate pipe dimensions. Quantity work combines accepted geometry with a justified allowance for settlement or compaction. A material list includes identity, size, quantity, units and drawing reference, not just an unexplained total.

sections.title: Define role of Grade Person
sections.text: The grade person transfers authorized control to usable offset stakes, marks and machine references. Protect the original control and record offsets so a stake displaced from the construction line is not mistaken for the line itself. Confirm benchmark identity, datum, instrument setup and backsight. If marks conflict or a stake moves, stop using it and obtain verification. Do not average conflicting elevations. Read back instructions with station, side, offset, target elevation and cut/fill direction.

sections.title: Perform typical calculations
sections.text: For differential levelling, height of instrument (HI) = known elevation + backsight; point elevation = HI − foresight. For grade, rise/run × 100 gives percent when both use the same units. A 2% crossfall across a 3.5 m horizontal half-width gives 0.070 m or 70 mm drop. Use a spirit level, builder’s level, laser and automatic slope control only with their setup, checking and operating instructions. Check calibration and an independent reference. Instrument displays do not make an incorrect benchmark correct. Record tolerances from the project rather than inventing a universal pass band.

worked.title: A level-book entry
worked.case: Benchmark EL 100.000 m; backsight 1.250 m; foresight to prepared base 1.670 m. Target base EL 99.650 m.
worked.solution: HI = 101.250 m. Existing base = 101.250 − 1.670 = 99.580 m. Target minus existing = +0.070 m: fill 70 mm at this point, subject to the specified material and compaction method. Check against the correct drawing revision and benchmark before directing work.

activities.prompt: Use the same benchmark with backsight 1.400 m and foresight 1.600 m. Target EL is 99.650 m. State cut or fill.
activities.answer: HI 101.400 m; existing EL 99.800 m; target − existing = −0.150 m, so cut 150 mm at the measured point.
activities.title: Use the same benchmark with backsight 1.400 m and foresight 1.600 m

activities.prompt: A profile uses horizontal 1:500 and vertical 1:50. Explain why measuring its apparent angle is unreliable.
activities.answer: The vertical scale is exaggerated ten times relative to horizontal. Calculate actual rise over horizontal run using dimensions and elevations. A screenshot may also be resized.
activities.title: A profile uses horizontal 1:500 and vertical 1:50

activities.prompt: Write a handover for a disturbed offset stake at station 0+080, right side.
activities.answer: Identify station, side, stake and observed disturbance; mark the reference as unverified, notify the grade/survey lead and request replacement or verification. Do not continue from an estimated mark.

practical: Set up and check spirit, builder’s and laser levels under supervision.
Verify automatic slope control against an independent approved reference.
Maintain specified grade and slope and retain a legible level-book record.
